transcript.text: Every so often when I put the washing machine on the whole kitchen power goes off and I have to go to the fuse box and flick the switch back up. It doesn't happen every time. Indesit, IWE 7 something.

This sounds like an earth fault causing your RCD (safety switch) to trip. The most common cause on Indesit machines is a failing heater element that develops a short to earth once it gets hot and wet. However, the drain pump or wiring could also be responsible. Please do not keep resetting the fuse if this happens again; repeated tripping can damage the appliance further. To help identify which part might be faulty, does the power go off immediately when you press start (before any water enters), or only later in the cycle once the machine has started filling and heating up?
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

It's not straight away - it's always a few minutes into the wash, on the 40 or 60 degree ones. It has never done it on cold, quick 30 or rinse and spin. I should say I've been resetting it each time, probably five or six times over the last month, no burning smell or scorch marks that I've seen.

[Heading: Heater element earth fault]
The fact that it only trips on hot cycles (40/60°C) and never on cold ones points strongly to the heater element developing an 'earth fault'. This is a common failure in Indesit machines and will not resolve itself; continuing to reset the fuse risks damaging your home's wiring or causing a fire. Please unplug the machine immediately. To confirm this, remove the rear panel (typically two screws), locate the large circular heater element at the bottom of the tub, disconnect its wires, and use a multimeter to check for continuity between the metal body of the element and each terminal screw. If you get any reading other than 'infinity' or 'OL', the element is faulty and must be replaced.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

I don't have a multimeter or an insulation tester, and I'm not comfortable taking the back off and working on the wiring myself. Is there another way to confirm it, or is this something I should get an engineer in for? I have unplugged it for now.

[Heading: Heater element earth fault requiring engineer replacement]
Since you are not comfortable with the testing, please leave the machine unplugged and call a qualified appliance engineer. This is a safety-critical issue; continuing to reset the fuse risks fire or electric shock. An engineer will need to open the machine, test the components safely with professional equipment, and replace the faulty part (most likely the heater element) before it can be used again.
